JSDoc parsing and annotation detection (REQ-JSDOC-PARSING, REQ-ANNOTATION-REQUIRED, error handling): - For @story (shared by require-story-annotation): src/rules/helpers/require-story-helpers.ts - jsdocHasStory(sourceCode, node): uses sourceCode.getJSDocComment and checks value.includes("@story"). - commentsBeforeHasStory(sourceCode, node): uses sourceCode.getCommentsBefore and checks for "@story" in values. - leadingCommentsHasStory(node): uses node.leadingComments to look for "@story". - hasStoryAnnotation(sourceCode, node): orchestrates jsdocHasStory, commentsBeforeHasStory, leadingCommentsHasStory plus imported helpers linesBeforeHasStory, parentChainHasStory, fallbackTextBeforeHasStory within a try/catch. - Guards against missing APIs and swallows errors, satisfying graceful handling of malformed comments. - reportMissing / reportMethod use hasStoryAnnotation() to avoid double-reporting when an annotation is present. - For @req (shared by require-req-annotation): src/utils/annotation-checker.ts - getJsdocComment, getLeadingComments, getCommentsBefore wrap ESLint SourceCode APIs and node.leadingComments. - commentContainsReq: checks comment.value.includes("@req"). - linesBeforeHasReq, parentChainHasReq, fallbackTextBeforeHasReq implement line, parent-chain, and raw-text window detection for "@req"; all have defensive guards and try/catch. - hasReqAnnotation(jsdoc, comments, context, node): - When sourceCode and node are available, first uses linesBeforeHasReq, parentChainHasReq, fallbackTextBeforeHasReq. - Falls back to jsdoc.value.includes("@req") or comments.some(commentContainsReq) when advanced detection is unavailable or fails. - Errors in heuristics are caught and treated as "no annotation" rather than breaking. - checkReqAnnotation(context, node, { enableFix? }): - Collects jsdoc and combined comments, invokes hasReqAnnotation. - If no annotation found, calls reportMissing(context, node, enableFix).

TypeScript support (REQ-TYPESCRIPT-SUPPORT): - Both rules explicitly support TSDeclareFunction and TSMethodSignature: - Visitors registered in require-story-visitors.ts for TSDeclareFunction and TSMethodSignature. - Listeners in require-req-annotation.ts for TSDeclareFunction and TSMethodSignature calling runCheck(node). - Detection logic uses the same shouldProcessNode and DEFAULT_SCOPE for these TS node types. - Tests use @typescript-eslint/parser to validate behavior on TS syntax (see below).

traceability.notes: The story requires two ESLint rules—require-story-annotation and require-req-annotation—that jointly enforce @story and @req annotations across the same set of function-like constructs, with shared scope/export configuration, robust JSDoc parsing, TypeScript support, clear error messages, and documentation. The implementation provides both rules as ESLint RuleModules, backed by shared helpers for DEFAULT_SCOPE, export priority, and node detection, ensuring that FunctionDeclaration, FunctionExpression, MethodDefinition, TSDeclareFunction, and TSMethodSignature are handled consistently while arrow functions are excluded by default. JSDoc and surrounding comments are parsed using ESLint SourceCode APIs plus additional line, parent-chain, and text-window heuristics, all wrapped defensively to handle malformed comments and locations. Both rules report errors at the function/method name node and supply clear, actionable messages and suggestions. Comprehensive RuleTester suites in tests/rules/require-story-annotation.test.ts and tests/rules/require-req-annotation.test.ts explicitly reference this story and exercise JavaScript, TypeScript, scope and exportPriority options, anonymous function handling, and error data. Rule documentation files describe behavior, options, and examples consistent with the story’s requirements. The rules are wired into the plugin’s dynamic rule loading and recommended/strict configs. Given this evidence and successful Jest invocation, all acceptance criteria and detailed requirements of docs/stories/003.0-DEV-FUNCTION-ANNOTATIONS.story.md are satisfied, so the story is assessed as PASSED.
